A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Raptor and Block-Recurrent Hypothesis research. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices A–F support a reliable comparison; the additional appendix material in v6 creates no material comparison gaps.

before.justification: v2 reports original Raptor benchmark results, training ablations, stochastic-depth experiments, and dynamical analyses, including Tables 1–2 and supplementary Figures 13–15.

after.justification: v6 retains these original benchmark, ablation, and dynamical-analysis results in the main text and appendices.

M1.justification: Max-cut partitioning, recurrent blocks, losses, and two-stage training are retained. Depth scaling already appears in v2 Section 3, Appendix A, and Table 2; v6 Appendix A.3 expands its implementation description without establishing a changed procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions retain CIFAR-100 experiments, ImageNet-1k classification and dynamics analyses, ADE20k segmentation, and NYUv2 depth estimation. No dataset, task, or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains DINOv2 ViT-S and ViT-B comparators. Figure 3 and Appendix B retain random contiguous and random non-contiguous partition baselines. The added citations do not introduce evaluated comparison methods.

E3.justification: Training budgets, layer partitions in Table 3, probe settings in Table 4, and dynamics protocols in Appendices C–D are unchanged. Appendix A.3 newly discloses initialization details without reporting a revision to an earlier setting.

E4.justification: The Table 2 component ablations and analyses of stochastic depth, overtraining, architectural controls, perturbation sensitivity, and layer swapping are retained. The expanded depth-scaling explanation adds no ablation or robustness experiment.

E5.justification: Both versions report three independently seeded Raptor runs with mean ± standard deviation in Table 1 and Figure 7, and ten sampled partitions per random baseline in Figure 3 and Appendix B. Uncertainty reporting practices are unchanged.

E6.justification: Numerical results and plotted findings match. For example, Table 1 retains k=3 results of 83.0±0.1 accuracy, 43.0±0.3 mIoU, and 0.618±0.006 RMSE. Table 2 and supplementary Figures 13–15 also retain their results.

T1.justification: The BRH definition, max-cut derivation, dynamical metrics, DMD formulation, and Levin-complexity claim and proof are unchanged. New Equations (4)–(7) spell out the existing depth-scaling implementation rather than introduce a theoretical result or revise mathematical reasoning.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution statements, and discussion retain the same claims about recurrent computational reuse, recovery of DINOv2 performance, and dynamical interpretability. Limited wording edits do not alter their scientific scope.

C2.justification: Interpretations of stochastic depth, angular attractors, token specialization, and low-rank dynamics remain unchanged. The discussion retains the need for causal studies at scale and the qualification that a residual performance gap remains.

D1.justification: New Appendix A.3 specifies the depth-scaling unity offset, final-projection Gaussian initialization with standard deviation 10^-4, and multiplication at the attention residual, MLP residual, and block output, including broadcasting. v2 supplied the MLP dimensions and activation but omitted these implementation details.

R1.justification: v6 adds Schwarzschild et al. (2021) on recurrence and depth, plus Raghu et al. (2021) and Nguyen et al. (2022) concerning representational block structure. These extend attribution in Sections 1–2 without substantially changing the paper's positioning.

P1.justification: v6 makes limited prose edits in Section 2, adds the Depth-Scaling Mechanism subsection and cross-references, and renumbers Linear Probe Fine-tuning from A.3 to A.4. The publication-status footer changes, while the overall narrative structure remains intact.

P2.justification: Figure and table designs and captions are retained. Local reflow moves Figure 4 upward and Table 4 downward; the added equations also split the end of Appendix E onto a mostly empty page. These are limited layout changes.

improvement.justification: Appendix A.3 resolves implementation ambiguity around the depth-scaling component already evaluated in v2, improving reproducibility. The three added citations improve attribution. These limited benefits outweigh slightly less compact appendix pagination; the empirical evidence, core claims, and theoretical arguments remain unchanged.
